shortQuestions: At Uhud the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the young Companions as well as the elders, and he accepted the opinion of the young men who wanted to go out of Madinah and meet the enemy in the open. He also gave young Companions important positions in the battle, which shows the trust and respect he gave to the youth.

The Holy Prophet (ﷺ) said that the example of himself and the prophets before him is like a man who built a beautiful house but left the place of one brick in a corner empty. People went round it, admired it and said, "If only this brick were put in its place!" He said: "I am that brick, and I am the last of the prophets" (Bukhari, Muslim). The hadith shows the finality of prophethood.

He spent his youth in honesty, purity and hard work. He grazed sheep, worked as a trader with Hazrat Khadijah's (رضی اللہ عنہا) goods, and was so truthful and trustworthy that people called him al-Sadiq and al-Amin. He kept away from the idol worship, drinking and games of the age of ignorance and helped the poor and the weak.

Many young people today are influenced by materialism, the media and fashion; they waste time, neglect prayer and respect for elders, and some fall into drugs, dishonesty and immodesty. In the light of the Prophet's (ﷺ) teachings youth should be truthful, modest, hard-working and kind, use their energy for learning and serving people, and make his Seerah their model.

In his youth he joined Hilf al-Fudul, a pact of the young men of Makkah to help the oppressed and protect travellers and the weak. He helped in the rebuilding of the Ka'bah and settled the dispute over placing the Black Stone peacefully, and he took part in trade and in helping relatives, orphans and the needy.

He said that modesty (haya) is a part of faith and that it brings nothing but good. For young people modesty protects their character: it keeps them away from indecency, controls their eyes, tongue and dress, and earns them respect in society and the pleasure of Allah.

He lived a very simple life: he slept on a mat of palm leaves that left marks on his body, mended his own clothes and shoes, helped in household work, and many days no fire was lit in his house for cooking — the family lived on dates and water. (Any one such instance from the text is a correct answer.)

He wanted to see youth who are strong in faith, truthful, modest and hard-working; who worship Allah from a young age (one of the seven under Allah's shade is a young man who grew up in His worship); who serve their parents and society, seek knowledge and are ready to sacrifice for Islam and the nation.
activities: Sample outline — The Love of the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) for the Youth of the Ummah: I. Introduction — youth as the strength of a nation; the Prophet's (ﷺ) special care for young people. II. Trust and responsibility — young Companions given leadership (Usamah bin Zaid commanding an army, Mus'ab bin Umair as teacher in Madinah, Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) on the night of Hijrah). III. Consultation and respect — accepting the opinion of the youth at Uhud. IV. Training and guidance — teaching manners to the young ("say Bismillah, eat with your right hand"), the hadith of seven under Allah's shade. V. Lessons for today — modesty, truthfulness, learning and service. VI. Conclusion.

Possible group findings — weaknesses: misuse of mobile phones and social media, wasting time, neglect of prayer and studies, disrespect to elders, impatience, imitation of foreign culture, drug addiction. Remedies: following the Seerah, good company, guidance by parents and teachers, sports and healthy activities, time management, religious and moral education, and positive role models.
